newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian interest rates to come down - RBI governor.
newsitem.headline: Indian interest rates to come down - RBI governor.

text.p: Indian central bank governor C. Rangarajan said on Tuesday that he expects interest rates in the country to ease in the next few months.
"I expect a softening of interest rates in the coming months," the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor told a conference on foreign investment.
He said "there have been signs of a decline in interest rates in the recent period, although much of these signs are at the short end" of the market.

He said the central bank's monetary policy aimed at ensuring an adequate expansion of credit to assist growth while achieving reasonable price stability in order to help promote savings, discourage speculation and keep the rupee stable.
He said bank deposit growth this year has been much stronger than last year, and it is expected that "credit availability from the banking system will considerably improve during the current year".
The RBI governor said "the pressure on (financial) resources will continue so long as investment intentions exceed domestic savings supplemented by foreign savings".
